title: Pinball Dungeon Crawl
pitch: Roguelike pinball dungeon crawl: a tiny wizard hunts a dragon's evil tome through a real machine's layered tables.

topics.title: Pitch
topics.summary: Roguelike pinball dungeon crawl: a tiny wizard hunts a dragon's evil tome through a real machine's layered tables.

topics.title: Player Fantasy
topics.summary: A tiny wizard searching for an evil tome held by an evil dragon.

topics.title: Pillars
topics.summary: 1. Never out of sight. 2. Every hit matters: real weight, always a step toward a goal. 3. Pure pinball: physics untouched, flippers only; the RPG happens in the abstract.

topics.title: Audience
topics.summary: Pinball people first, plus some roguelike die-hards. A short-to-medium game. When needs clash, make it feel like pinball.

topics.title: References
topics.summary: Yoku's Island Express is close, but that's a side-scroller. This looks and works like a real pinball machine, and is very mechanical.

topics.title: Core Loop
topics.summary: Shoot, break mobs for gold. Quest spawns new mobs; break them and a dungeon opens. Drop in, beat the encounter, hit 1 of 3 loot targets or exit, pop back up, next quest.

topics.title: Core Mechanics
topics.summary: Pure pinball. Each flipper carries 1 item with an impact effect. Picking loot replaces the item on the last flipper to touch the ball; exiting takes nothing.

topics.title: Controls & Feel
topics.summary: Flippers only. No extra button: spells and weapons come from flippers or are passive on the ball.

topics.title: Goals
topics.summary: Complete 3 tiered dungeons in order, ending at the dragon's lair. Light quests open each dungeon and can change the field or open micro dungeons.

topics.title: Challenge
topics.summary: Targets have health and armor. Early damage takes 1 fewer hit on unarmored, normal on armored. Shot order changes because of RPG effects.

topics.title: Failure & Recovery
topics.summary: Permadeath: 1 wizard, 3 lives from the amulet; an item or two can add a life. Any drain, including in a dungeon, costs a life and wipes both flipper items and gold. Next ball, same map.

topics.title: Progression
topics.summary: No XP. Progress is dungeon completion, which unlocks the next tier, plus loot. Early items are simple benefits, never wrong to hit; higher-level loot can be game changers.

topics.title: Rewards & Economy
topics.summary: Hits earn gold. Dungeon loot is 1 of 3 choices or none. 3 shops with an item on top: shoot the one you can afford, ball is held, press a flipper to drop to that side and equip it there.

topics.title: Setting
topics.summary: Pinball dungeon crawl: towns, quest givers, dungeons, all inside a machine.

topics.title: Story
topics.summary: Told by dot-matrix text and table changes. After dungeon 2 the dragon returns to its lair: landscape ruined, flames, 2 random town buildings destroyed and 2 left open, new trash mobs, a quick trick shot opens the lair.

topics.title: Characters
topics.summary: The ball is the tiny wizard. The evil dragon holds the tome.

topics.title: World & Level Structure
topics.summary: Built vertically: main table on top, dungeon tables reached by rails, each with its own flippers and a sealed exit until the encounter is beaten. Town block is an inn + 3 shops. 3 dungeons per run, 3 types per tier. Terraforming unproven.

topics.title: Opposition
topics.summary: Bosses start as moving, evading targets. Breakable mobs, random-encounter spawns, puzzles (trick shots, ordered targets). Final boss: the dragon, with 3 lair layouts using different mini bosses and trash mobs.

topics.title: Art Direction
topics.summary: Looks like a real 3D pinball machine, very mechanical: metal wire rails, tables stacked vertically, rails going transparent as the ball travels.

topics.title: Audio & Music
topics.summary: All real old-school pinball sounds.

topics.title: UI & HUD
topics.summary: Everything on the dot-matrix display. If that doesn't work well, use an overlay.

topics.title: Camera
topics.summary: Whole main table on screen. Entering a dungeon: the rail turns transparent, camera follows and zooms as the ball rolls in from the top side, showing the table for 2-3 seconds, then settles into a pinball view.

topics.title: Onboarding
topics.summary: The first quest teaches it: dot-matrix says something like BREAK THE GOBLINS, targets flash, first dungeon is easy. The rest is introduced one piece at a time.

topics.title: Session Shape
topics.summary: Maybe 15 minutes a run. Unlike real pinball, there's a goal that ends the game, so the player is trying to finish, not just last. Worth exploring.

topics.title: Replayability
topics.summary: Random loot and 3 dungeon types per tier. No carry-over between runs so far. Light terraforming from a few presets: use more if good, stay fixed if meh.

topics.title: Accessibility
topics.summary: Prototype baseline: only two buttons, remappable keys, ball speed option, and a dim mode that softens the machine lights.

topics.title: Platform & Tech
topics.summary: Engine open: Godot or C++. Option under discussion: 3D visuals, with each table its own 2D physics plane and rails as scripted paths.

topics.title: Scope & MVP
topics.summary: Full idea stays the vision. First prototype: one main table, one dungeon, a few flipper items; no terraforming or dragon. Tests hit feel, rail drop and camera, loot choice.

topics.title: Business Model
topics.summary: Free portfolio piece: both the design docs and the prototype.

topics.title: Risks
topics.summary: Physics feel, camera work, content load (9 unique dungeon tables), terraforming breaking tables.
